name_reason: Already follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (fd2_play_palette_ prefix matching its sister fd2_play_palette_fade_in), accurately describes the behavior (VGA palette fade-OUT to black), and carries no Ghidra address residue -- 'play', 'palette', 'fade', 'to', 'black' are all semantic words. No domain-ID suffix involved.
purpose: VGA palette fade-OUT from full brightness to black, used as the 'fade out' hook on chapter end / cinematic exit / ending transitions.
logic_summary: for subtract = 0 .. 0x3F (0x40 iterations): fd2_set_vga_palette_range(0,0xFF,subtract) writes the full DAC range as max(0, base[i]-subtract), then fd2_delay_ms(2) (2 BIOS ticks ~110ms each). subtract=0 -> base palette (full brightness); subtract=0x3F -> all channels clamped to 0 (black). Loop progresses FULL -> BLACK = fade-OUT. In the binary this entry is a shared-body wrapper: it XORs the counter to 0 and JMPs into the darken loop body (0x1F503-0x1F524) physically living inside fd2_load_and_fade_in_cinematic_image @ 0x1F81E; Watcom regenerates an equivalent standalone loop in the source. Counterpart of fd2_play_palette_fade_in @ 0x1F525 (fade-IN, subtract 0x40..0).

returns.semantics: No return value; side effect is reprogramming the VGA DAC over ~7 seconds to darken the screen to black.

Comment fix replaced em-dash->'--' and arrow->'->' only within this symbol's block (lines 349-368); other non-ASCII lines (2,261,299,300,389) belong to OTHER symbols and were left untouched (out of single-symbol scope).
